11.t: Working with data: bone marrow transplants
q: Calculate the percentage increase in survival with a matched sibling transplant compared with chemotherapy only.
Explain how a bone marrow transplant can treat leukaemia.
Chemotherapy destroys the cancerous marrow; the donor marrow contains stem cells that divide and differentiate into all the healthy blood cell types.
Describe and explain the relationship between donor match and graft-versus-host disease.
The poorer the match, the more often it happens (15% to 40%). Donor T-cells recognise the patient’s cell-surface proteins as foreign and attack the patient’s tissues.
Explain why the result for the partly matched group is less reliable.
Only 40 patients: a small sample, so chance has a bigger effect.
Suggest why a brother or sister is the most likely good match.
They have the same parents, so they may inherit the same tissue-type alleles (a 1 in 4 chance of a full match).
Calculate the surface area of the 2 cm cube, and the SA : V of the 0.5, 1 and 2 cm cubes.
Describe the relationship between SA : V and the percentage coloured.
The higher the SA : V, the larger the percentage coloured: from 35% at 2 : 1 to 100% at 12 : 1.
Explain why the 0.5 cm cube is fully coloured but the 3 cm cube is only 35% coloured.
Acid diffuses in through the surface. The small cube has much more surface per unit volume and a short distance to its centre.
Use the results to explain why cells are small.
Cells take in oxygen and nutrients and remove waste across their surface; in a large cell the centre would not be supplied fast enough.
Suggest two ways large organisms overcome the SA : V problem.
Any two: flattened or folded surfaces (villi, microvilli); specialised exchange organs such as lungs; transport systems like blood.
